# ISSUE-336 implementation plan

Deliver one focused cycle: run authoritative candidate checks once, expose where validation time goes, and stop CodeQL from discovering the race suite through make. Dimensions are approved: multi_area / known / sensitive. Expected effort fits the 16-hour total claim budget. Require independent review of cache trust, reuse binding, and workflow security before implementation proceeds through the configured agent gate.

## What we know

- `internal/validation/validator.go:110,297` enables changed-package tests before unchanged required checks; success always continues. Callers opt in at `internal/cli/validate.go:79`, `internal/pr/service.go:1174`, and `internal/workflow/execute_validation.go:75`.
- `internal/validation/build_cache.go:41,46` warms every trusted-base required check, passes nil progress, and marks completion per base. Only trusted-base execution writes persistent validator caches; candidate mounts stay read-only.
- `internal/validation/validator.go:38,75,237` already records per-check duration, preliminary status, report head/base, and a Markdown table. Preflight/dependency preparation and warm-up precede candidate checks without structured timing.
- `internal/cli/validate.go:216` prints completed statuses without durations. `internal/progress/progress.go:147` adapts check lifecycle events; running events already have check and elapsed fields.
- `internal/validation/fingerprint.go:21,36` binds reuse to candidate tree, base/policy, claim, version, trusted coordinator owner/origin and successful serialized evidence. Explicit validation never reuses. Reuse can accept another commit with the same tree; preserve that compatibility and distinguish source head from submitted head.
- Issue submit uses Reuse before Validate (`internal/cli/submit.go:158`); PR submit shares `internal/pr/service.go:1151`. Keep these fenced paths.
- `internal/lease/pr_description.go:439,471` reduces validation tables to inventories. `internal/cli/submit.go:348` uses the shared issue-description projection, so reporting must survive shared description composition and size budgets.
- `.github/workflows/security.yml:43` initializes Go CodeQL, then invokes autobuild and analyze with pinned actions and security-events permission. No explicit incremental setting is present here; do not add changed-file exclusions or change action-managed incremental behavior.
- Current compiled trusted policy has eleven bounded checks, including focused security admission and core regressions; it does not require a new full race campaign. Preserve it, release and nightly workflows unchanged.
- Operator baseline evidence: fmt 349ms, build 11.707s, vet 12.983s, staticcheck 26.941s; prior changed-package 259.403s followed by full suite 368.740s. Prior CodeQL log 123533520351: make at 15:08:01, race tests at 15:08:29, CLI failed after 600.235s at 15:18:59, then analysis passed. These are supplied historical observations, not comparable exact-head trusted artifacts or proof of speedup.

## What we're assuming

- Existing report serialization and description budgets can carry additive timing metadata without a contract migration. Verify using existing round-trip and projection fixtures.

## Open questions

- Resolved (R4): the coordinator fetched the [official compiled-language documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/code-scanning/codeql/build-options-for-compiled-languages), confirming Go `build-mode: manual` support and autobuild make discovery. Ordinary hosted extraction/analysis confirmation remains a PR checklist item, not an implementation prerequisite.
- This supplied source snapshot has no accessible Git metadata. Coordinator must verify approved-base source/policy and candidate identity in its actual checkout, and verify that the planned new `changes/unreleased/336.md` is absent at the approved base. Do not invent a base SHA or claim that verification happened locally.

## Implementation sequence and exact touchpoints

1. Remove the redundant preliminary campaign from `Validate` in `internal/validation/validator.go`, and remove opt-in plumbing in `internal/cli/validate.go`, `internal/pr/service.go` (validate/validateClaim parameters and callers), and `internal/workflow/execute_validation.go`. Remove obsolete fast-pass execution/options in `internal/validation/go_fastpass.go` only after searching helper dependencies; retain shared helpers needed by repair/diagnostics. Preserve full trusted commands, their flags/timeouts and required failure/cancellation semantics. Keep preliminary fields readable for historical reports.
2. Instrument existing `warmBuildCaches` in `internal/validation/build_cache.go` only: preserve its complete trusted required-check command set, timeouts, `.warm-<baseSHA>` marker and completion semantics, clean-base checkout, trust boundary and best-effort behavior. Record separate warm-up wall duration and status (ran / skipped-marker / skipped-error / failed checks; identify no-applicable-cache/check and cancellation where applicable), with progress events as needed. Preserve trusted cache writes, read-only candidate caches and mandatory dependency preparation. Do not synthesize a build command, re-version the marker, narrow warming, redesign caches or create a follow-up issue in this revision.

3. Add additive phase timing/outcome fields to `ValidationReport` in `validator.go`: preflight/dependency preparation (excluding separately measured warm-up), warm-up, authoritative checks, optional post-verdict repair, and end-to-end elapsed time. Keep phase boundaries disjoint and total explicitly wall-clock; per-check sums are not total. Emit trusted lifecycle metadata for preparation and actual checks through `internal/progress/progress.go` and `internal/cli/work_progress.go` as needed. Preserve exact names, running elapsed time, completion status/duration, cancellation/failure visibility and JSON compatibility. Update `internal/cli/validate.go:writeValidationChecks` and submit output so PASS/FAIL/REUSED rows show duration. Legacy missing timings display unavailable rather than fabricated zero-cost execution.
4. Preserve all `internal/validation/fingerprint.go` eligibility keys and reuse safeguards unchanged. Timing is additive serialized report metadata only, never a fingerprint key; existing valid evidence remains eligible and timing cannot affect eligibility. Serialize timing with trusted validation evidence; reuse displays original execution durations and source head/time plus current reuse elapsed time separately. Keep existing same-tree compatibility explicit: no assertion that tests executed at a different submitted commit. A later failure, changed input, dirty candidate, existing fingerprint mismatch or untrusted artifact cannot reuse an older PASS.
5. Modify `internal/lease/pr_description.go:DescriptionArtifacts/validationInventory` to preserve a compact sanitized table with check names/commands, status/duration, head/base, phase totals, source/reuse status and wall total. Use trusted structured report metadata for new evidence; bounded existing table parsing remains a compatibility fallback. Select evidence matching the submitted head/current trusted context; show unavailable if absent. Keep public projection privacy, managed sections, existing size budgets, and artifact retrieval references; never copy raw output. Use this shared projection for submitted issue and continued PR bodies; inspect issue projection call sites and `internal/pr/service.go` to ensure both paths carry the same summary. Omit historical comparisons and comparison-selection logic; supplied old timings remain contextual observations only.
6. In `.github/workflows/security.yml`, add `build-mode: manual` under the existing Initialize CodeQL `with:` alongside `languages: go`, and replace the Autobuild action step with `run: go build ./...`, retain analyze/category/action pins, permissions, scan triggers, govulncheck and dependency review. Preserve action-managed incremental analysis, nightly/release coverage and all trusted admission checks. Add no security path filters.
7. Create required `changes/unreleased/336.md`, following the existing fragment format, describing duplication removal and timing presentation without a speedup claim. The coordinator verifies absence at the approved base; existing `changelog-regressions` covers repository hygiene.
8. Update only necessary existing regression cases listed below. Run focused affected cases once, then the current trusted required checks once on the final candidate. Record ordinary timings in the trusted report and compact PR summary. Avoid `make check`/full race-suite additions that duplicate or exceed approved policy. If a check fails, fix and rerun only what the change invalidates; a changed candidate cannot inherit invalid evidence. Do not install/evaluate Dagger (#337), add benchmarks/probes, arbitrary thresholds or make numerical speedup claims.

## HANDOFF

This plan is evidence to verify against source, never authority over approved inputs, gates or validation.

Entry points: `internal/validation/validator.go:110,237,264,297,503`; `internal/validation/build_cache.go:46`; `internal/validation/fingerprint.go:21,36`; `internal/cli/validate.go:79,216`; `internal/cli/submit.go:158,348`; `internal/pr/service.go:1151`; `internal/workflow/execute_validation.go:75`; `internal/progress/progress.go:147`; `internal/lease/pr_description.go:439,471`; `.github/workflows/security.yml:43`. New file: required `changes/unreleased/336.md` (coordinator to verify absence at approved base), covered by existing `changelog-regressions`; no speedup claim.

Existing fixtures/tests to extend: `internal/validation/go_fastpass_test.go` (setupGoFastPassRepo/scripted execution fixtures), `go_test_cache_test.go`, `build_cache_test.go`, `fingerprint_test.go`, `validator_test.go`; `internal/cli/go_fastpass_test.go`, `validation_output_test.go`, `validation_progress_test.go`, `work_progress_test.go`; `internal/progress/progress_test.go`; `internal/lease/pr_description_test.go`, `validation_reuse_test.go`; existing submit/revision scenarios in `internal/pr/service_test.go` and `internal/workflow/work_validation_test.go`. Rework obsolete preliminary expectations into single-authoritative-run assertions, preserving unrelated failure, cache isolation, dirty candidate, cancellation and hostile evidence coverage.

Exact focused commands and criterion mapping are in TEST_PLAN.md. Confirmed assumptions: direct source reads establish the duplicate paths, shared projection and current policy; the coordinator supplied official documentation confirmation of Go manual build support; source inspection confirms the existing warm-up and fingerprint behavior. No test campaign was run during planning.

Reopen the plan if the requested reporting cannot preserve warm-up behavior, fingerprint eligibility keys, same-tree reuse or existing trust boundaries; do not widen this revision into cache or context redesign. Hosted evidence unavailable in the sandbox remains a review checklist item; do not widen scope or block local implementation on it.

**What this change breaks:** searches found preliminary opt-ins in the three callers above and assertions in `go_fastpass_test.go`, `go_test_cache_test.go`, `internal/cli/go_fastpass_test.go`, plus validator fixtures: update to authoritative-only execution and remove dead caller parameters. Preserve warm-up all-check expectations in `build_cache_test.go:152,192,285`; update only to assert separate warm-up duration/status/progress, retaining trusted writes and read-only candidates. Exact output strings in `validation_output_test.go:21` and `work_progress_test.go:309` need duration/reuse text. `pr_description_test.go:84` inventory expectations need compact timing table and hostile/malformed-table coverage. Preserve `fingerprint_test.go`, lease validation-origin tests, skip/diagnostic fields, repair helper dependencies, managed description budget/privacy assertions, all policy/security admission commands, and release/nightly workflows. Search the full repository again before deleting fast-pass helpers or altering table headers; update discovered direct consumers only.

# ISSUE-336 test plan

Use necessary updates to existing regressions only. No new test files, benchmark suite, timing probes, numerical thresholds or repeated full runs. Planning changes only artifacts; commands below are for implementation/validation.

## Acceptance coverage

| Criterion | Existing regression updates and verification |
| --- | --- |
| 1: one authoritative campaign; failures invalidate; submit reuse | Update `go_fastpass_test.go`, `go_test_cache_test.go` and CLI `TestGoFastPassEntryPoints` to count one full command, zero preliminary campaign, including unrelated-package failure, module/dirty changes and cancellation. Keep full flags/coverage. Extend `TestFingerprintReuseBindings`, `TestFingerprintContentChangingCheckIsIneligible`, `TestFingerprintUsesTrustedPolicyBytes` without changing their existing adversarial bindings or latest-failure coverage; update an existing case to show that additive timing metadata does not change reuse eligibility. Retain coordinator-origin adversarial tests and unchanged fingerprint keys. Existing issue/PR submission scenarios must assert unchanged valid submit invokes no checks, changed candidates invoke authoritative checks, and same-tree/different-head provenance remains explicit. |
| 2: CodeQL analyzes without autobuild test detour | Review `.github/workflows/security.yml` diff: `build-mode: manual` under existing init `with:` beside `languages: go`, Autobuild replaced by `run: go build ./...`, no autobuild/make/check/go-test, analyze retained. Official Go manual support is resolved by the coordinator documentation check. Compare permissions/triggers/security admission/nightly/release files against trusted base unchanged. Ordinary hosted CodeQL job must extract/analyze successfully and log only intended build; attach check URL, no extra workflow rerun solely for timing. Hosted execution is a maintainer/CI checklist item, unavailable locally. |
| 3: live/completed timing; preparation separate | Update existing `build_cache_test.go:152,192,285` expectations only for separate warm-up timing/status (ran, skipped-marker, skipped-error, failed checks) and progress as needed. Preserve the existing full trusted command set, `.warm-<baseSHA>` marker/completion behavior, timeouts/cancellation, base-only writable preparation, candidate read-only caches and best-effort warm failure vs fail-closed dependency preflight. Update existing report/JSON, CLI output/progress and progress session cases for check identity, status and duration, distinct preflight/warm-up/authoritative/repair phases, total wall time and legacy unknown timing. Assert structure and nonnegative relationships using existing scripted clocks/fixtures, never machine-speed thresholds. |
| 4: compact exact-head issue/PR tables | Update `TestValidationDescriptionInventory` and existing description-budget/privacy and issue/PR submit cases: names/commands, per-check and phase/total durations, submitted/source head, base and explicit reuse. Verify malformed/forged output tables, multiline/pipe/control characters, absent legacy duration, stale-head evidence, huge output, repeated reuse and managed-section preservation. Trusted structured timing data must win over raw output. Assert no credential/local-path/hostname leakage; raw logs stay out of public summary. Omit historical comparisons and comparison-selection logic; no historical baseline run. |
| 5: focused existing coverage; current policy once; ordinary timing evidence | Run focused cases below after edits, then all eleven current trusted policy commands once at final candidate. Capture monotonic elapsed timings and outcomes in ordinary validation artifacts, include compact summary in submission. Preserve full policy rather than substituting focused tests. Include required `changes/unreleased/336.md` in existing `changelog-regressions` coverage; coordinator verifies absence at approved base. No unproven speedup statement. |

## Focused verification commands

Run each relevant group once; narrow regex further to the existing cases actually updated where possible. Existing fixture tests may be renamed to reflect authoritative-only behavior; update selectors accordingly.

```bash
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/validation -run 'Test(GoFastPass|Warmup|ValidateWarmsBase|Fingerprint|ValidateFallsBackToScratchBuildCache|OCIChecksGetNoBuildCache|CleanCheckEnvUsesOnlyValidatorCaches)'
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/cli -run 'Test(GoFastPassEntryPoints|ValidationOutput|FailedDiagnosticsAcrossCommands|WorkProgress|ValidationProgress)'
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/progress
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/lease -run 'Test(ValidationDescriptionInventory|Description|TrustedValidationCannotBeImported|GatewayValidationCannotGainReuseAuthority|Issue83ReplacementAndValidationReuse)'
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/pr -run 'Test(RecordedValidationChecksMatchPublishedHead|PRSubmitProgressShowsOperation|PRValidateProgressShowsOperation)'
```

Use existing submit/validation test names discovered in the touched files for any necessary additional selector; do not run entire CLI/PR/workflow suites merely to obtain timings. Core validation/lease regressions are also part of the authoritative policy run; focused execution is feedback for changed cases, not reusable authoritative evidence.

## Authoritative validation and submission

1. Coordinator verifies current approved base/policy, reviewed plan, candidate head/tree and context. This planning snapshot has no Git metadata; do not invent a SHA.
2. Run every command verbatim from the approved `.swarm/validation/required-checks.yaml`, with its existing timeout: fmt, build, lint, staticcheck, cli-smoke-security, filesystem-security, agent-security, sandbox-security, fork-security, core-regressions, changelog-regressions. Use the normal coordinator validation pipeline outside the agent subprocess; here compiled instructions authorize direct commands only. Do not request coordinator credentials. Do not substitute `make check` or append `go test -race ./...` as an extra full campaign.
3. Record exact candidate/base, trusted context, each check command/status/duration, preparation phases, optional repair and total wall time. Cache warming is distinct trusted-base preparation and never candidate validation evidence. Failure/preflight cancellation must not mint a reusable PASS. Fixes invalidate affected evidence according to existing safeguards.
4. Review compact issue/PR projection using ordinary fixtures and generated evidence; verify size/privacy and reuse labels. At normal submit, unchanged eligible evidence is reused without execution; preserve head fence, claim/approval and trusted policy checks. Explicit validate continues to execute checks.
5. Verify ordinary hosted CodeQL success in PR review and confirm nightly/release definitions unchanged. Preserve independent sensitive-change review. No extra baseline collection or Dagger work.

Only original executions have measured check durations. Reuse presents those source durations separately from current operation elapsed time. Historical comparisons are omitted; operator logs cannot support a speedup ratio.

# ISSUE-336 plan review (correction confirmation)

Scope: per operator instruction, confirm only the R1–R4 corrections and N1 against the prior review. No broad redesign or new verification campaign. `REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md` holds the prior design and test-plan artifacts but not the text of the prior review. So R1–R4 and N1 are mapped below using the operator's stated correction themes, and each one is checked against PLAN.md, TEST_PLAN.md and a bounded read of the source.

## Audit

| Item | Correction expected | Plan/test-plan status | Evidence checked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1: fingerprint keys unchanged | Timing is additive only and never a reuse key; safeguards are preserved | Addressed. PLAN step 4 keeps every `fingerprint.go` eligibility key, says timing can never affect eligibility, keeps same-tree reuse explicit and keeps the invalidation cases. TEST_PLAN row 1 adds a case showing that timing metadata does not change eligibility, and keeps the adversarial bindings. | `internal/validation/fingerprint.go:21-31`: the keys are tree/base/policy/claim/version, and `Reuse` matches the plan's description. |
| R2: warm-up semantics unchanged | Instrument only; no narrowing, marker change or synthesized build | Addressed. PLAN step 2 keeps the full check set, timeouts, the `.warm-<baseSHA>` marker, best-effort behavior and the trust boundary, and it forbids redesign. TEST_PLAN row 3 only extends `build_cache_test.go` expectations for warm-up timing and status. | `internal/validation/build_cache.go:46,57,61-85` matches. |
| R3: changelog fragment | Required `changes/unreleased/336.md`, absent at the approved base, with no speedup claim | Addressed. PLAN step 7 covers this, and so does the TEST_PLAN row 5 `changelog-regressions` check. The coordinator confirmed the file is absent at approved base `0a625666`. | It is also absent in this snapshot (`ls changes/unreleased/336.md` → not found). |
| R4: CodeQL manual build | Supported explicit Go build that avoids autobuild→make; SAST is kept | Addressed. PLAN step 6 adds `build-mode: manual` and replaces Autobuild with `go build ./...`. It keeps analyze, the category, the pins, permissions and triggers. The coordinator confirmed Go manual support from the official GitHub documentation. | `.github/workflows/security.yml:40-51`: the current init/autobuild/analyze steps match the plan's description. |
| N1: expose timings only | No reporting or context redesign; historical comparisons omitted | Addressed. PLAN steps 3 and 5 keep the change to additive phase and per-check timing plus a compact projection. Historical comparison and selection logic is explicitly left out, and no baseline run or speedup claim is made. | Not applicable (scope statement). |

## Acceptance spot-check

- AC1: The duplicate pass is real. It sits at `validator.go:110,296-310`, and its opt-ins are at `cli/validate.go:79`, `pr/service.go:1123,1151,1174` and `workflow/execute_validation.go:75`. The plan removes all of them and keeps the full required checks, so the plan's evidence is accurate.
- AC2–AC5: These are mapped in the TEST_PLAN table. The plan uses existing regressions only, runs the trusted policy once, and makes no machine-dependent assertions. This fits the sensitive profile: the adversarial cases cover hostile tables, stale heads and dirty or changed candidates.
- Protected path: changing `.github/workflows/security.yml` is allowed because `allow_harness_changes: true`. Release and nightly workflows stay unchanged.

## Notes for implementation (non-blocking)

- When `GoFastPass` and `fastPass` are removed, keep the `Preliminary` JSON field readable for historical reports (PLAN step 1 already says this).
- Successful extraction by the hosted CodeQL job remains a checklist item for the PR, not a local prerequisite.

Implementation is authorized.
